newsitem.title: UK: South Beach Cafe plans AIM debut and expansion.
newsitem.headline: South Beach Cafe plans AIM debut and expansion.

text.p: Health-conscious cafe group South Beach Cafe Plc said on Wednesday it plans to raise 1.8 million stg in a flotation on the London Stock Exchange's Alternative Investment Market (AIM) scheduled for May 27.
The company, previously listed on the OFEX share trading system run by brokerage JP Jenkins, is expected to have a market capitalisation of 9.7 million stg at the issue price of 6p per share.

South Beach has opened two art-deco style cafes on the campus of Michigan State University and a third in London's Baker Street. Two are under development in London and Sarasota with two more planned in London.

The prospectus for the issue shows the group made a pre-tax loss for the 10 month period to December 31 1996 of 367,000 stg but Tom Burnham, South Beach's chief executive, said he was "delighted" with the performance in the current year so far.
Burnham said the proceeds from the flotation would be used to expand the number of cafes and for extra working capital.

The group said it has developed a new American food concept, centred on bagels and spreads, speciality coffees, fresh fruit smoothies and veggie drinks. Its menu in the cafes includes veggie drinks such as carrot, beet, spinach, celery and wheatgrass and chicken dijon bagels.
Burnham devised the recipes which he described as an interesting experience but more time consuming than he originally anticipated.
"You just get the flavours for the veggie drinks a little bit wrong and the taste goes way off," Burnham said.
